hypotheses.title: macro_gamma_regime_flip
hypotheses.theoretical_basis: Dealer gamma positioning (GEX) dictates market stability. High macro-volatility (measured via Treasury spreads) triggers dealer re-hedging, which can flip the market from a 'stabilizing' (positive gamma) to a 'destabilizing' (negative gamma) regime, accelerating price moves.
hypotheses.hypothesis: When the rolling 5-day volatility of the 10y-30y spread exceeds its 20-day mean AND the aggregate SPY Gamma (GEX) is approaching zero, SPY 1-day forward volatility will expand significantly.
hypotheses.signal_definition: Calculate Net GEX for SPY: SUM(options_eod.gamma * options_e_od.open_interest * options_e_od.underlying_price) grouped by date. Calculate Treasury Vol: STDDEV(treasury_rates.10y - treasury_rates.30y, 5) / STDDEV(treasury_rates.10y - treasury_rates.30y, 20). Signal triggers when GEX_ratio < 0.1 and Treasury_Vol_Ratio > 1.5.
hypotheses.compute_approach: Step 1: Query treasury_rates to compute 5d and 20d stddev of (10y-30y). Step 2: Query options_eod for SPY to aggregate weighted gamma. Step 3: Compute the ratio of GEX to its 20d mean. Step 4: Identify dates where Treasury_Vol_Ratio > 1.5 and GEX_ratio < 0.1. Step 5: Measure SPY IV change in following 24h.
hypotheses.expected_edge: High. Captures the structural transition from mean-reverting to momentum-driven regimes using macro-proxies.
hypotheses.novelty: Combines fixed-income volatility (ELINT/SIGINT) with equity derivatives microstructure (SIGINT).

hypotheses.title: informed_sweep_divergence
hypotheses.theoretical_basis: Large-scale 'sweeps' in the options market represent informed participants (HUMINT) acting on information before it is reflected in the broader crowd sentiment (CAG). A divergence between aggressive flow and crowd awareness indicates an impending price breakout.
hypotheses.hypothesis: When the volume of 'BUY' side sweeps in flow_trades (premium > 100k) increases by 3x its 10-day mean while the 'CAG' (Crowd Awareness Gap) in signal_values remains low, the underlying asset will experience a positive price drift.
hypotheses.signal_definition: Identify flow_trades where side='BUY' and premium > 100000. Compute 10-day rolling mean of sweep_count. Compare current_sweep_count / mean_sweep_count. Cross-reference with signal_values.ticker='SPY' AND signal_name='CAG' where value < threshold.
hypotheses.compute_approach: Step 1: Aggregate flow_trades by date/symbol for premium > 100k. Step 2: Compute 10d rolling mean of this count. Step 3: Fetch CAG value from signal_values. Step 4: Trigger signal if (Current_Count/Mean) > 3 AND CAG < 0.2.
hypotheses.expected_edge: High. Detects 'hidden' institutional positioning before the 'crowd' (CAG) reacts.
hypotheses.novelty: Uses real-time trade intensity (SIGINT) to find information asymmetry in crowd sentiment (HUMINT).

hypotheses.title: rv_iv_convergence_lead
hypotheses.hypothesis: When the spread between Realized Volatility (RV) and Implied Volatility (IV) reaches a 20-day extreme, the IV will revert to the RV, predicting a volatility expansion or contraction.
hypotheses.signal_definition: Compute 5-day RV from prices_daily.year_change(close). Compute 30-day ATM IV from options_eod.iv. Signal = (RV - IV) / STDDEV(RV - IV, 20).
hypotheses.compute_approach: Step 1: Calculate 5d rolling stddev of prices_daily.close. Step 2: Fetch 30d ATM IV from options_eod. Step 3: Compute the spread. Step 4: Z-score the spread against a 20-day window. Step 5: Predict direction of IV based on Z-score magnitude.
hypotheses.expected_edge: Medium. Exploits the predictable mean-reversion of the volatility risk premium.
hypotheses.novelty: Focuses on the 'discrepancy' as a predictive feature rather than just the level of volatility.

hypotheses.title: liquidity_shock_hawkes_proxy
hypotheses.theoretical_basis: High-frequency trading activity follows a self-exciting (Hawkes) process. A sudden cluster of trades (liquidity jump) in the options market often precedes a liquidity-driven volatility spike in the underlying equity.
hypotheses.hypothesis: A spike in the frequency of 'sweep_id' occurrences in flow_trades within a 15-minute window, followed by an increase in the bid-ask spread (from flow_trades.bid/ask), predicts an increase in options_eod.iv.
hypotheses.signal_definition: Count unique sweep_id in flow_trades per 15m window. Calculate spread_expansion = (flow_trades.ask - flow_trades.bid) / flow_trades.bid. Signal = (Count_Zscore > 2) AND (Spread_Expansion_Zscore > 2).
hypotheses.compute_approach: Step 1: Group flow_trades by 15m intervals. Step 2: Compute frequency of sweep_id and mean spread. Step 3: Apply Z-score transform to both metrics. Step 4: Identify simultaneous spikes.
hypotheses.novelty: Uses trade-level 'burstiness' as a proxy for the self-exciting nature of liquidity shocks.

hypotheses.title: bond_equity_vol_lead_lag
hypotheses.hypothesis: Volatility in the 10y Treasury yield leads volatility expansion in the S&P 500 (SPY) with a 1-to-3 day lag.
hypotheses.signal_definition: Calculate 5d rolling stddev of treasury_rates.10y. Calculate 5d rolling stddev of options_eod.iv for SPY. Signal = Correlation(Treasury_Vol_t-n, SPY_IV_t) where n in [1,3].
hypotheses.compute_approach: Step 1: Compute rolling volatility for 10y yields. Step 2: Compute rolling volatility for SPY IV. Step 3: Use a cross-correlation function to find the lag (n) that maximizes the correlation coefficient.
hypotheses.expected_edge: Medium. Leverages the cross-asset lead-lag effect documented in high-frequency research.
hypotheses.novelty: Quantifies the specific lag-time of macro-to-equity volatility transmission.
